pageCache.pageTitle: RGS Guildford | Independent Day School in Guildford, Surrey
pageCache.text:
Royal Grammar School Guildford (RGS) is an independent day school in the heart of Guildford, Surrey, educating pupils aged 3 to 18. Founded in 1509, we combine more than 500 years of heritage with a confident, forward-looking approach to learning — and from September 2027 we will welcome girls, becoming fully co-educational with phased entry across the school.
Our school spans three connected stages. RGS Prep, half a mile from the senior school, nurtures children from Nursery and Reception through to Year 6. RGS Senior offers a rigorous, wide-ranging education for students aged 11 to 18 from our historic High Street site. And our Sixth Form prepares young people aged 16 to 18 for the very best universities and for life beyond them.
What unites every stage is a kind, inclusive community where high achievement and genuine character go hand in hand. Inspiring teachers, exceptional facilities and a programme of more than 70 clubs and societies give each pupil the space to discover what they are capable of.
Whether you are looking for a prep school, a senior school or a sixth form in Guildford, we would love to welcome you. Come and see RGS Guildford for yourself.
A balanced, big-hearted school where enjoyment of learning is evident; you’d be hard pressed to match the education on offer here.
Read our inspection reports
Co-education
We are excited that the RGS will become co-educational, offering girls the same opportunities that our boys have enjoyed for centuries: academic enrichment and challenge, diverse co-curricular experience and outstanding pastoral care. Girls will be welcomed into both RGS Prep and RGS Senior, with phased entry from September 2027.
Future Ready
Academic excellence sits at the heart of everything we do, and our consistently strong results reflect it, but they are only part of the story. As a leading independent school in Surrey, we pair inspiring teachers and excellent facilities with a genuine focus on the world beyond our gates. Our students leave with real academic prowess and with the collaboration, confidence and critical and creative thinking they will need to thrive at university and in their careers.
Just as importantly, life beyond the classroom – through sport, music, the arts and our wider co-curricular programme – helps children to grow into capable, grounded young people, ready for whatever comes next.
Co-curricular
Life beyond the classroom matters just as much to us as what happens within it. We dedicate real time to our co-curricular programme. Monday afternoons and five Field Days (off timetable enrichment days) across the Senior School, and our Inspire Programme and Activities Week throughout RGS Prep.
With more than 70 clubs and societies spanning sport, music, drama, the arts, academic societies and outdoor pursuits, there is something for every interest and every ambition. Along the way, students develop the self-reliance, leadership and teamwork that characterise an RGS education and stay with them long after they leave.
Our Values
We are proud of our kind, inclusive community where diverse opportunity, personal development and high achievement define who we are, and where our Values of Inclusivity, Scholarship, Integrity, Respect, Courage and Collaboration underpin all that we do.
Learn more about Our Values

pageCache.pageTitle: Art, DT, Music & Drama | Sixth Form Surrey | Royal Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Art
We encourage all our students to participate in some form of creative pursuit which they do with exceptional skill and imagination, enthusiasm and enjoyment. There is a real sense of creative freedom and opportunities exist for each individual to explore their passions, resulting in our students developing a true appreciation of the Arts.
Imagination, along with problem-solving and project-based work, create students who can think on their feet and have the confidence to formulate their own ideas and see things through to their conclusion. The Arts provide an outlet for the expression of thoughts, feelings, and observations, and they do this with impressive maturity and insight.
Design & Technology
Much like our Art School, the Design & Technology workshops are bright, airy and inspiring environments. A focus on mastering techniques allows our students to develop self-expression at their own pace as well as a passion for innovative design.
Our teachers are professional practitioners who work in their studio classrooms so that the students can benefit from their expertise and demonstrations. Our practicals allow the students to gain hands on experience using a wide variety of tools and machinery. The range of work created, including sculpture, woodwork, metalwork, mixed media and more traditional art forms, clearly illustrates the breadth of talent. Our corridors and display areas provide a living gallery, inspiring generations of students and visitors alike.
Music
The breath-taking talent of our students is fostered in an environment where they can fully express themselves, irrespective of their passions. High-profile and more intimate performances, frequently as shared initiatives with local girls’ schools, promote personal expression.
Our Music Department has established an admirable reputation, exceptional by any school’s standards. It is rare to walk through the Old Building at any time of day without hearing the inspiring sounds of music. A host of choirs and ensembles, supported by a staff of passionate musicians, caters for all abilities and interests.
The School offers individual tuition on singing and pretty much every and any musical instrument. In fact, over 300 one-to-one music lessons take place in any one week. Regular concerts and recitals locally, nationally and internationally allow the students to showcase their musicality in surroundings as atmospheric as the historic courtyard of the Old Building and as impressive as St Mark’s Basilica in Venice.
Drama
Drama is a vibrant and energetic part of the life of the School. Plays cater to all age groups, from the more intimate to the most ambitious performances, including joint school musicals and productions with local girls’ schools.
In the last few years, productions have included Bugsy Malone and Les Misérables, The Little Shop of Horrors, Emil and the Detectives and Oliver! From developing performance skills through LAMDA and professional workshops, to technical theatre including lighting, sound, set construction and stage management, our passionate Drama Department encourages every student to express themself creatively: working collaboratively, building confidence, and supporting the journey of self-expression.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art, DT, Music & Drama | Prep School Surrey | RGS Guildford
pageCache.text:
Art
Any visitor to RGS Prep will immediately be struck by the variety and quality of art on display. Everyone who pauses to examine the works will be impressed by the individuality of character showcased by these displays.
The teaching and learning in this subject aims above all to stimulate an individual expressive response of the chidren’s own ideas, values, and viewpoint.
Creative projects in clay, felt, papier maché, card, paint, chalk, pencil, collage and wire allow the pupils to see their imaginations realised in physical form. The theme might be universal but experimentation is keenly encouraged.
The Art Department is among our most active in organising trips to exhibitions, galleries, and activity centres to ensure the boys gain the widest possible appreciation of what art means, and what it means to make it.
Browse our art & design booklet for more information
DT
Our DT programme fosters innovative thinking and aligns closely with the senior school’s GCSE and A Level pathway, equipping students with skills vital for future studies. Students are timetabled for a double lesson every week, which allows plenty of time to learn and get stuck in with practicals. Our specialist teachers present engaging, hands-on lessons that encourage the students to use both their creativity and technical skills for design solutions.
The workshop is equipped with advanced tools and machinery which, with careful instruction, students as young as 9 years old can explore. Through research and design, manufacturing, and evaluation, our carefully crafted projects encourage students to take calculated risks and follow the full DT process. The students also participate in non-construction projects including coding, computer-aided design (CAD), and computer-aided manufacture (CAM), all of which are important skills in the ever-increasing technological age.
Outside of timetabled lessons, we provide lunchtime DT drop-in sessions, internal workshops, field trips, House competitions, enrichment activities on the weekends, and opportunities to work with other local schools.
Browse our art & design booklet for more information
Drama
All pupils enjoy drama as a subject in its own right. Drama nourishes the imagination and nurtures spontaneity. Children develop their understanding of the processes of dramatic playing, role-playing, improvising, process drama, play building, interpreting scripts, rehearsing and directing.
Drama also embodies inclusivity; every pupil is given an opportunity to explore their own creative skills in their weekly drama lessons to the well-planned presentations and productions. Taught as a specialist subject, drama allows the children to experiment with their use of body language, facial expressions, use of the voice and to engage in a variety of drama skills giving shape to a polished performance. We also have our own performance space, lighting and sound desk, costumes and props store.
Browse our drama booklet for more information
Music
Supported by a rich programme of training, ensembles, choirs, and orchestras, all led by specialist musicians, all our pupils are encouraged to explore their musical potential.
They perform in an array of concerts, services, festivals, competitions and galas. Many routinely gain distinctions in the higher ABRSM Grades and join county and national groups. Our Maestro programme prepares our finest musicians for scholarship. RGS Prep is the choir school of Guildford Cathedral, with a long tradition of providing boy choristers for professional services throughout the year. Our choristers receive rigorous, first class musicianship training from the cathedral and many have gone on to become professional musicians.
Take a look at the booklet below which gives details of our music curriculum, instrumental music lessons, ensembles, bands and choirs and performance opportunities within our school.
Browse our music booklet for more information

In the nurturing environments of Nursery and Reception (Shell), our primary focus is to provide an environment which is positive, inclusive and safe. Within the Early Years, we are committed to providing a diverse range of stimulating, practical activities which allows each child to learn through firsthand experiences.
Tailored Learning Environment
Young children are naturally lively and curious about the world around them. As we welcome girls alongside boys, our learning environment is designed to spark that curiosity in every child: dynamic, hands-on and interactive, and tailored to how our youngest learners thrive.
The Curriculum at RGS Prep
We follow the statutory framework provided by the Department for Education for Early Years providers, and our approach supports learning and development from birth to five years old.
Communication and Language: Rich opportunities to listen, talk and build vocabulary, through stories, songs, discussion and imaginative play, lay the foundations for confident speaking and early reading.
Literacy: Daily phonics, shared stories and plenty of mark-making develop early reading and writing, moving gently from a love of books in Nursery to more formal phonics and handwriting in Reception (Shell).
Maths: Practical, hands-on activities introduce number, shape, pattern and measure, alongside the mathematical language children need to reason and solve simple problems.
Understanding the World: Children explore the natural world, their local community in Guildford and the wider world, developing curiosity through first-hand experiences and our outdoor learning programme.
Expressive Arts and Design: Art, music, dance and role-play give children the freedom to create, perform and express their ideas, supported by specialist teaching.
Personal, Social and Emotional Development: Through our buddy system, House activities and School Values, children learn to build friendships, manage their feelings and grow in independence.
Specialist lessons: From Reception (Shell), children also enjoy weekly Spanish, dedicated music, art and drama with subject specialists, PE on the Prep School grounds and a weekly swimming lesson.
Classroom Learning
Pupils begin their learning for the two-year rolling topic in their classrooms. They delve into specific themes such as the Arctic, building a comprehensive understanding over time and developing a foundation for future learning.
Outdoor Learning
Pupils enjoy frequent visits to our Outdoor Learning area, where they take part in activities that consolidate their classroom learning as well as everything from roasting marshmallows over the firepit to building minibeast houses.
We recognise the value of practical activities in the Early Years. Engaging with the natural environment enhances cognitive and sensory experiences, while hands-on activities build motor skills and problem-solving abilities. Outdoor activities foster creativity, imagination and social skills.
Co-Curricular
Beyond the curriculum, pupils enjoy engaging trips and events, and an extensive clubs programme. Learn about our co-curricular opportunities and wraparound care here.
Transition – moving up to Year 1
Because our Nursery, Reception (Shell) and Years 1 to 6 all sit within RGS Prep, children move through the early years and into Key Stage 1 and 2 without changing school. Our dedicated Pre-Prep building ensures that our youngest learners are always in familiar surroundings with Early Years and KS1 teachers to look after them.
Nursery children step up into Reception already familiar with our staff, routines and grounds; and as Shell pupils move into Year 1, they carry those friendships and learning habits with them. It is a settled, confident journey through the founding stage of an RGS education.
Throughout Pre-Prep, our pupils regularly make use of the facilities of the Prep school across the road ensuring that they move onto Key Stage 2 confident in themselves, their learning and their environment.

Curriculum FAQs
What curriculum does the Nursery follow?
Our Early Years provision follows the statutory EYFS framework, covering the seven areas of learning through play based and child led activities.
What specialist lessons are included?
Music and games from Nursery, with Spanish, art, drama and swimming added in Reception (Shell).
What are the class sizes?
Our Early Years classes are small, with a class teacher and teaching assistant in every class. Typically a ratio of 1 adult to 8 children is the norm.
How is my child's progress assessed?
Children are observed and assessed in line with the EYFS framework. We regularly share pupils work and progress via our online app, in teacher: parent meetings. In Nursery we encourage parents to visit for a Stay and Play session where the children can show you what they have been learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast Club & Wraparound Childcare, Guildford | RGS Prep
pageCache.text:
We know that family mornings and evenings can be busy, so we offer wraparound childcare for Nursery and Reception children from 7.30am through to 6.30pm, Monday to Friday. From a calm breakfast to relaxed after school play, your child is well cared for from the moment they arrive until you collect them.
Breakfast Club: from 7.30am, with porridge, fruit, cereal and toast.
Before School Care: drop off from 8.00am.
After School Care: From the end of the day until 4.30pm we offer childcare within the school fees. After this time our external provider, ActivSport provides After School Care with a range of fun activities and a healthy snack until 6.30pm.
Breakfast Club and After School care are booked directly with ActivSport. Applicable fees can be found on this link Book a Class | ActivSport
Breakfast Club
We welcome pupils from Nursery & Reception to the Prep Dining Hall for Breakfast Club Monday- Friday from 7.30am. We offer nutritional food options including porridge, fruit, cereal and toast.
The perfect calm start to the children’s busy and fun-filled days at school. Breakfast club offers welcoming wraparound childcare. Pupils are excited to see their friends when they arrive and enjoy joining the rest of their classmates at 8.15am to begin the days learning.
Before School Care
With little ones, we understand that mornings can be very busy. We are pleased to offer drop off from 8.00am where Reception pupils can unpack their belongings in their classroom and then enjoy a run in the playground with their classmates.
Nursery children can be dropped straight to the Nursery where they enjoy a wide range of supervised activities to ease our young learners into their day. We provide activities that stimulate both social and cognitive development, to assist with a smooth transition from home to the school environment.
After School Care
After school we provide activities such as Kapla Club and Playball for pupils in Reception. All Early Years pupils can access the late class from 3.20pm where a variety of activities is provided.
From 4.00pm until 4.30pm, things slow down and the children have access to quieter activities to help them relax after a busy day. After 4.30pm, the children are taken over to the Prep school to join the main After School Care club run by ActivSport. Here they are provided with a healthy snack and can be picked up any time up until 6.30pm.

pageCache.pageTitle: Years 1 - 6 Curriculum | Private School Surrey | RGS Guildford
pageCache.text:
With a careful balance between academic, creative and physical lessons, as well as teacher-led and pupil-led learning, children are able to develop and grow through first-hand experience and a range of stimulating activities.
Learning across the curriculum is enhanced through a comprehensive programme of trips, visits, workshops, themed days and extra-curricular clubs.
Children are engaged in their learning, make good progress and build secure relationships.
Years 1 & 2
At RGS Prep we are committed to developing a creative curriculum with a mixture of interesting topics, themed weeks and projects to motivate our children in their learning. The curriculum offers a broad content of study, using the National Curriculum (Key Stage One) as a basic framework.
The combination of group work activities and high individual attention promotes appropriate learning for all children across levels of ability. KS1 pupils build upon the EYFS curriculum that was introduced in Nursery and Reception (Shell). Our pupils extend their learning in many ways and are given varied opportunities to explore the curriculum. Topics are introduced with a cross curricular approach.
Our Key Stage One children show high levels of independence, curiosity, and concentration. They are enthusiastic about coming to school and enjoy the detailed educational programmes organised to reflect their varied and imaginative needs.
The class teacher is the appointed key person for the children’s pastoral welfare and educational progress during their time at Pre-Prep. Classroom assistants support the class teacher in this role.
Years 3 to 6
As in the earlier years, the National Curriculum is only part of the school’s own curriculum which covers a broad spectrum of academic, physical, creative and artistic experience to challenge the mind and develop personal interests and skills.
Through a rich curriculum, children are given the opportunity to expand their subject knowledge, reinforce their numeracy, literacy and ICT skills, as well as develop effective learning strategies through the RGS Prep learning habits.
In Year Three to Six, lessons are taught by both form teachers and specialist subject staff, making full use of our excellent facilities. In addition to the broad curriculum offered in KS1, Spanish, Latin, Verbal and Non-verbal reasoning are introduced from Year Five.
Pupils are mostly taught in mixed ability classes across the curriculum. Children are streamed from Year Four in mathematics and ability sets are introduced in English in Year Six.

pageCache.pageTitle: Cathedral Choir | Primary School Guildford | Royal Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Guildford Cathedral Choir School
RGS Prep is proud to be the Guildford Cathedral Choir School. The boy choristers of the Cathedral Choir (a separate group of girl choristers was formed in 2002), are all educated at RGS Prep. They rehearse at school on four mornings a week, and the full choir of boys and men sings at Evensong in the Cathedral on Tuesdays and Thursdays; there are currently three choral services on Sundays.
There are also duties at Christmas and Easter. The main activity of the choir is the maintenance of regular sung services, but in the last few years the choir has also toured in Normandy, Bruges, the East Coast of the USA and most recently, the Netherlands. The choir has given concerts locally and in London, has made several recordings, and has appeared on BBC Radio 3.
Full details can be found here
Most days there’s a good chance you’ll hear the melodic voices of the boys at their morning practise.
Vacancies
There are vacancies each year for musical boys who are interested in becoming choristers; the Chapter of the Cathedral award educational bursaries to boys selected for the choir.
Future Careers
Many choristers go on to pursue careers in music, and all benefit from the experience of teamwork and sense of achievement the choir gives them; in particular, ex-choristers often go on to achieve music scholarships and other awards at leading schools.

In January 2025, the RGS was inspected by ISI (The Independent Schools Inspectorate) in which the School was recognised for having not one but two significant strengths in the educational experience. We are one of just a small handful of schools in the whole country to receive two Significant Strengths, a rare distinction that is awarded if a school demonstrates a clear, measurable, and profoundly positive impact on its students.
A school culture that actively promotes inclusion and mutual respect highly successfully. This is a significant strength of the school.
Pupils develop a breadth of knowledge and enthusiasm for scholarship. This is a significant strength of the school. This strong academic culture leads to pupils who readily engage in critical thinking and deep learning and display intellectual curiosity.
Pupils develop social skills, confidence and self-esteem, ensuring they are well prepared for life.
Tolerance, kindness and mutual respect pervade every aspect of school life.

The happiness and welfare of every child lie at the heart of what we do. In our Nursery and Reception in Guildford, we shape our wellbeing programme around the needs of our youngest learners, so they feel known, safe and cared for from their very first day.
Leaders prioritise and support pupils’ physical, mental and emotional health well.
Pupils feel well-supported in school.
A robust safeguarding culture across all parts of the school.
Emotional Check-Ins
In Nursery and Reception, students engage in an emotional check-in with their teachers at the beginning of each day, expressing their feelings through discussions related to the story of the Colour Monster and identifying when they feel the same. This provides a quick, non-verbal communication method for pupils and helps our staff identify those who may need some extra support.
Our Buddy System
The buddy system pairs younger students with pupils in Key Stage 1, promoting positive role modelling, empathy, and friendships across Year Groups.
Physical Education & Outdoor Learning
Recognising the importance of physical activity in promoting positive mental wellbeing, our Early Years pupils have a lesson with specialist games staff each week using the facilities in the Prep school, and sessions on the astro at Pre-Prep. Beyond sports, pupils enjoy our Outdoor Learning area, a delightful space for exploration and learning about nature through hands-on activities.
Wellbeing Events
We host a Wellbeing Week in support of Children’s Mental Health, featuring activities such as mindfulness crafts, silent discos, and joke-telling. Our annual Hygge Day, celebrating the Danish concept of creating a warm atmosphere, invites pupils to wear cosy clothes and bring their soft toys.
PSED & Additional Support
Our PSED curriculum helps our pupils to recognise their feelings and others, understand behaviour and build relationships. The curriculum also equips pupils with knowledge on staying safe and provides guidance on who to approach if they encounter any issues. For those needing additional support, we offer drawing and talking therapy, targeted assistance, and the expertise of an Emotional Literacy Support Assistant (ELSA).
Safeguarding
Mr Freeman-Day, the Head of RGS Prep, serves as our Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL), supported by several Deputy DSLs, including Mr Moore (Deputy Head), Mrs Petersen (EYFS Coordinator), and Mrs Self (Head of Wellbeing).

pageCache.pageTitle: Partnerships | Independent School Surrey | Royal Grammar School
pageCache.text:
RGS Guildford has forged many strong and long-lasting external relationships with local, national and international organisations in order to engage in meaningful partnership and outreach activities. We are extremely proud of all we have achieved via reciprocal engagements with our partners, yet continue to seek and be open to new sustainable connections for the benefit of all.
We take great pride in the provision of a wide variety of opportunities for pupils to contribute to the lives of others both within the school and in the wider local, national and international community.
Local Primary and Secondary School Partnerships
Locally, RGS Guildford provides a varied and exciting programme of enrichment activities with local primary and secondary schools, is an associate member of the Learning Partners Academy Trust (LPAT), and a member of the Guildford 11-19 Partnership and works with other HMC schools and the Independent Schools Council regarding partnership working.
Local Community Partnerships
Our students volunteer their time and talents to serve our local community during our extra-curricular and General Studies programmes. Each week Sixth Form students coach sport, run chess clubs, and teach maths to local primary school pupils;
they provide maths enhancement sessions for Kings College pupils; they visit Abbots Hospital to document residents’ stories; and they labour at the Rosamund Community Garden. They also help at a long list of events to which we invite students from the wider Guildford area such as the RGS Masterclasses, Careers Convention, society lectures, author visits, drama performances, and engineering competitions, to name a few.
International Partnerships
Our charitable International Links partnerships continue to forge and develop meaningful relationships which increase our students’ understanding and experience of the wider world.
Joint expeditions to Southeast Asia
These support the work of educational charities to promote education in rural areas and enable our students to visit, teach and work in these less developed communities. Though these expedition and partnerships are challenging and ambitious, they are often one of the highlights of students’ memories of their school days: the camaraderie, the personal challenge and the enrichment mean the value of such experiences is an intrinsic part of their development.
We are committed to supporting two schools in Besisahar in the Lamjung District of Nepal. A key pillar of the partnership is our student and staff exchange visits with us hosting selected Nepali students and staff in Guildford and RGS and Tormead joint expeditions to visit Besisahar. Our fundraising activities have provided significant funds to enable the development of the library and science facilities at Bhu Pu School.

At RGS Guildford, our academic reputation is complemented by an equally vibrant and diverse curriculum in Drama, Music, Art, DT and Sport, ensuring a holistic and enriching educational experience for our students.
Pupils develop a breadth of knowledge and enthusiasm for scholarship. This is a significant strength of the school.
First and Second Form Curriculum
Our curriculum offers access to all the aesthetic, human and social, linguistic, mathematical, creative and literary, scientific and technological, physical and moral and spiritual areas of learning. By studying a range of subjects, our students are able to make informed option choices and forge their bespoke path which plays to their individual strengths and passions.
Core Language (French/Spanish/German)
Third to Sixth Form Curriculum
As they move up the school a degree of optionality is introduced into the curriculum, allowing students to begin to narrow their focus on fewer subjects.
Learning Habits
Central to a lifelong love of learning, and interwoven throughout each student’s curricular and co-curricular experiences, the RGS Learning Habits are the behaviours and attributes which students develop, helping them to thrive as they progress through school, university and beyond.

being fiercely curious and intellectually inquisitive;

Our Move to Co-Education
Throughout its rich 500-year history, the School has always innovated to build on our success. Our focus is always solely on what is in our students’ best interests, educationally and with regard to their wellbeing and personal development. We firmly believe that co-education now provides us with an opportunity to enhance the education we provide to the benefit of all.
We want an RGS education to be reflective of today’s society – one where equity and equal opportunity for the sexes are promoted and in which both girls and boys are able to have equally ambitious aspirations, to work collaboratively and to set themselves up for fulfilling, enriching, happy futures.
The RGS has rich history of providing the very best education for boys, and RGS students have for many years enjoyed regular interactions and developing lasting friendships with their peers from local girls’ schools: travelling to and from school together, co-performing in drama productions and music concerts, enjoying joint trips and expeditions, learning together through the General Studies programme in the Sixth Form, and enjoying both organised social events and also meeting informally in town. Our move to co-education is a natural step for us, and as a co-educational community we will enrich the educational experience of all our students and the preparation we provide them for university and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clubs & After School Care | Prep School Surrey | RGS Guildford
pageCache.text:
There’s a head-spinning number of extra curricular sporting (and non-sporting) clubs also on offer.
Clubs
Our Clubs programme, which includes Before and After School Care, is comprehensive and extremely diverse offering over 50 clubs and activities providing our pupils with fun, learning and enjoyment beyond the School Day.
Every term, parents receive a booklet detailing what clubs are on offer the following term and then make their selection using our online booking form. We try to ensure that pupils have the opportunity to experience all of their chosen clubs, and, in instances where a club is over-subscribed, we operate a waiting list system which gives them priority the following term.
Browse our clubs booklet to learn more
Breakfast Club & After School Care
At RGS Prep we offer wraparound care before and after school. Breakfast Club, which includes nutritional food, is available for all pupils from 7.30am each day at a daily cost of £6.75 per session.
There is also an after school class in both the Pre-Prep and Prep Years at no extra cost. Pre-Prep can book into lates until 4.30pm and Prep can book in for pick-up at 4.45pm. There is further after school provision run by a company called ActivSport, which is open after lates, until either 5.30pm or 6.30pm. This can be booked directly through ActivSport’s website.
Holiday Clubs
Camp Beaumont
Camp Beaumont are hosted either at RGS Prep or the RGS throughout half terms and end of term holidays (excluding Christmas). Pupils at the school can benefit from discounts on bookings. Look out for information with discount codes in our regular parent communications. For more information click here.
Playground2Pro
P2P is a multi-sports camp offered to RGS Prep pupils during school holidays. A typical day with P2P is divided into 6-8 sessions, each lasting 30 to 45 minutes and tailored to all age groups and abilities from Year 1 to 6.

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior Staff | Senior School Surrey | RGS Guildford
pageCache.text:
Our Senior Management Team (SMT) provides the leadership that shapes every aspect of school life, implementing the School’s vision and upholding high standards. The SMT work closely with the whole staff body to create an inspiring, supportive environment for all.
Senior Management Team
Dr JM Cox
As Headmaster of RGS Guildford, Jon has been instrumental in driving numerous initiatives aimed at enhancing the academic and extracurricular offerings of the School.
His leadership is characterised by a strategic vision that balances tradition with innovation, ensuring that the School remains at the forefront of educational excellence. His passion is to make the RGS accessible to all pupils and, as a consequence, the creation of an enduring bursary fund has been as focus of his leadership.
Under his guidance, RGS Guildford has continued to thrive, maintaining its reputation as one of the leading independent schools in the UK, while also emphasising the importance of traditional values and outstanding pastoral care.
Mr AU Woodman
Adrian Woodman joined the school in 2004 as a Teacher of Biology and has since become a central figure in its leadership and wider community. For the past twelve years he has served as Senior Deputy Head, a role in which he oversees the pastoral life of the school and contributes significantly to whole‑school strategic development. He also deputises for the Headmaster when required and firmly believes in the values of character education for all young people.
Throughout his time at the school, Adrian has played an active role in the co-curricular programme. He has particular interests in rugby, cricket and tennis, and for many years served as a Flying Officer in the RAF section of the Combined Cadet Force. His breadth of experience includes several key pastoral positions: Deputy Head of Sixth Form, Head of Middle School, and later Head of Upper School upon joining the Senior Management Team.
Adrian brings extensive expertise in safeguarding, having served as Designated Safeguarding Lead for over a decade. He was also instrumental in shaping and developing the school’s Learning Support Department, ensuring that provision for pupils with additional needs is robust, compassionate and forward‑looking.
Outside school, Adrian enjoys spending time with his family. Together they can often be found playing sport, cycling, or exploring the countryside on long walks.
Mrs JSR Thorpe
Jill began her teaching career in 2004 in South Devon before moving to Surrey. Jill worked in co-ed schools in the state sector for 12 years in a variety of roles, teaching Biology, Head of KS3 Science, Outdoor Education, Head of Vocational Education and joined RGS Guildford in 2016. She is passionate about enabling students to reach their full potential and enabling staff to have the autonomy to deliver the best education for students.
Outside of work, Jill enjoys sailing and has been a National Coach Assessor and International Centre Inspector. She also ran the county’s Search and Rescue team, still a current operational member she attends callouts as a dog handler and as a search manager.
Mr JW Pressley
Jimmy joined RGS Guildford in 2000 from KCS Wimbledon, and also has experience of teaching in co-educational schools, in both the state and independent sector. He has held various leadership positions at the RGS including Head of Classics, Head of Sixth Form, Assistant Head and Senior Master; he has also coached most sports during his time at the School. Within the classroom he strives to inspire a love of learning and to instil a passion for classical languages; in his leadership roles, he takes pride in upholding and promoting the School Values and strong sense of community at the RGS to current – as well as prospective, and past – students and parents.
Outside of work, family – including his three sons – and friends, travel, fitness, the Surrey countryside and pubs, and supporting home and away his beloved Brighton & Hove Albion fill his time.
Mr ST Maiden
As Chief Strategy Officer, Sam is responsible for strategy development and delivery across all parts of the RGS, including RGS Guildford and our wider international family of schools. His focus is on helping the RGS to innovate and embrace the future, whilst ensuring it stays true to its ethos and values. He brings over 25 years of experience of leading complex change, including previous senior positions in both the charity sector and management consultancy.
Outside of work, Sam is passionate about sport and is mostly to be found on a touchline somewhere, supporting his children whilst trying to remain un-biased. He is also a keen amateur cook, and enjoys walking in the Surrey Hills with his family.
Mrs RF Whitham
Becky is the Director of Finance and Operations, with responsibility for finance, HR, IT, health and safety, estates, and governance—where she also serves as Clerk to the Governors. She enjoys the variety and challenge of the role and is committed to making sure everything runs smoothly behind the scenes, so staff can focus on what they do best and students have the best possible experience.
Before joining the school sector, Becky spent 17 years working in universities in London and the south coast, leading operational teams and overseeing strategic planning. Her most recent role was as Director of Operations at UCL, focussed on their advancement programme. Outside of work, she has a young family, so much of her spare time is spent at clubs and activities, but she loves to travel whenever the opportunity arises.
Mr NW Gough
Nick joined the RGS back in 2008 fresh out from finishing his MSC in International Relations and Economics. As an economics teacher who trained at RGS and Guildford County School, he has held a variety of different roles at the RGS including: Head of International Partnerships, Head of Economics and Head of Upper School before starting his current role leading safeguarding and pastoral care in 2023. Nick enjoys leading a busy pastoral team that is always looking to help students develop as individuals within the kind and diverse community that is the RGS.
Away from work, Nick’s passions include sport, travel and development education. This has led him to own a rusty tuk tuk, currently stationed in his back garden that once travelled with him and a former RGS teacher through 38 countries!
Miss NS Goul-Wheeker
Natacha gets huge satisfaction from supporting all teachers with their classroom practice, whether they are new to the profession or more experienced. She enjoys staying up-to-date with the latest educational research and then exploring how best to put this into practice within our school context. She firmly believes that through self-reflection, collaboration and engagement with research, teachers can continually refine their practice to deliver an exceptional experience for all their students. She is equally interested in how best to support students in developing their own learning habits to ensure they reach their highest potential both at school and beyond.
Natacha has been responsible for Teaching and Learning since 2016, having previously held pastoral roles at the school. Before joining the RGS, Natacha taught at a similarly selective co-ed independent school. Outside of school, Natacha enjoys playing tennis and running, as well as spending time with her young family.
Mr TW Shimell
Following reading a MChem at Oxford University, and PGCE at Cambridge University, Tom joined the teaching profession in 2003 teaching Science a variety of schools from London to New Zealand. Tom joined the RGS in 2007 where, in addition to teaching Chemistry, Tom has held a variety of roles leading Teacher Training, Head of Fifth Form, Head of Sixth Form and, since 2016, Assistant Head Partnerships. Tom passionately believes in working with talented colleagues at RGS as well as local primary and secondary schools to create exciting educational opportunities for all students in our wider community.
Tom is passionate about holistic education and the role that co-curricular and, in particular, outdoor education play in our lifelong character development and Tom leads the Royal Naval Section of the CCF, teach dinghy sailing, and provides tuition and support for Gold DoE expeditions.
Outside of work, Tom enjoys training for and competing in triathlon events and can usually be found in the pool/lake/sea, or running or cycling through our beautiful Surrey countryside. When not being a ‘Dad-taxi’, he enjoys a garden project, puzzles, escape rooms and playing board games with his family.
Mr DSJ Wright
David joined RGS Guildford in 2012, following his first career in banking and finance. He is an enthusiastic teacher of Economics and former Head of Department. As a member of the leadership team, David’s goal is to ensure all pupils meet their academic potential whilst studying a rigorous, forward-looking curriculum designed to spark curiosity and inspire a lifelong love of learning.
David spends all the time he can outside of work, outside. A keen watcher and coach of rugby, walker in the hills and mountains, reader, birder and dog-lover, he has given up on technology and plays golf with vintage clubs.
Mr SJH Yetman
Steve joined the Geography Department in 2001, teaching across all year groups for nearly two decades. During this time, he developed a particular interest in Geographical Information Systems and established a reputation for bringing innovative, real‑world applications of geography into the classroom.
A strong advocate for character development and a holistic approach to education, Steve has played a central role in shaping the school’s Co‑Curricular programme throughout his career. His contributions have been especially influential in the area of outdoor education. He expanded the sailing programme into the Middle School games curriculum, introduced the Royal Naval section to the Combined Cadet Force, and oversaw the development of the school’s ski race training programme. He also founded the Third Form Expedition and Adventure (EXAD) programme, designed to build resilience, teamwork, and a sense of adventure in younger students.
Alongside his work within the School, Steve also gives significant time to national school sport. He volunteers as a board member of the English Schools’ Ski Association, helping to guide the strategic development of competitive school skiing in the UK. In this capacity, he organises squad race training in Norway for boys and girls from schools across the country, providing opportunities for young athletes to develop their skills in a high‑performance alpine environment.
Mr MJ Royds
Mike works with our international schools to develop living partnerships across the family of schools, following experience in high-performance schools both in the UK and overseas. Alongside experience leading in A Level and International Baccalaureate curricula, Mike has enjoyed positions of academic, pastoral and house leadership. His experience overseas includes early planning for a school transitioning into a co-educational environment; more recently in the UK, he was Head of Upper School in the RGS.
Along with a love of working with people and making connections, Mike is at his happiest outdoors. Fortunately, his family share his enthusiasm for the outdoors and even put up with his attempts at various musical instruments.
Dr AJ Morrison
Alastair is Managing Director of RGS Guildford International, the team that oversees and sets up RGS Guildford international schools, all of which are co-educational. This includes maintaining quality and managing the relationships with our partners and schools in China, Dubai, Oman, Qatar and India (opening in 2028), as well as pursuing opportunities for new schools in other markets overseas. Alastair has held senior leadership positions in international partnerships over the last fifteen years in the heritage and higher education sectors, and is a passionate believer in the transformative impact that international experiences and perspectives can have on students and staff.
Having lived and worked in China and Italy, Alastair speaks five languages and brings a truly global outlook to his work. Outside of his professional role, he enjoys cycling, hiking, sea swimming, and exploring the countryside both in the UK and overseas.
Heads of Section
Mr MF Baggs
Having returned to the RGS in 2022, Matt is now in his fourth year of his role as Head of Lower School, having been Director of Sport at King’s College School, Wimbledon and Caterham School. In both of these schools, he held the position of Director of Sport, overseeing both the girls and boys sport programmes. Prior to that, Matt ran the hockey programme here at RGS from 2010 to 2016, as well as holding the positions of Deputy Head of House and Head of Lower Sixth, Deputy Head of Sixth Form. Matt brings a breadth of knowledge from his experience in different schools across Surrey, allied to his depth of understanding of the RGS and its core values.
Matt is passionate about using education to develop character, individuality and seeks to create an environment where every student matters. He firmly believes that happy students make successful students and works with the extensive pastoral team to ensure that each and every student is supported in the way that works for them to allow them to thrive. Having been on more than 50 school residential trips in his career, he is a firm believer in a broad and varied co-curricular provision being a core part of an outstanding education.
Outside of work, Matt is an avid sports fan, keen cook and enthusiastic traveller, though most of his time outside of work is now spent enjoying the company of his two daughters whilst transporting them from one activity to the next! Matt also has much to thank the RGS for, having met his wife on the staff in his first stint at the School.
Mr JC Witts

pageCache.text:
Thank you for your interest in the RGS. We very much look forward to welcoming you through our doors to experience what makes the RGS such a vibrant, welcoming and inspiring environment.
From September 2027 the RGS will become co-educational, welcoming girls alongside boys into our school in Year 12. In September 2028 we will welcome our first intake of girls to Year 7. The transition will then progress organically through the year groups. If you’d like to know more about our move to co-education please take a look at our brochure.
Information about our admissions process can be found below. For questions or queries about any aspect of the admissions process please contact Admissions on 01483 880 600 or by email at RGS-Admissions@rgsg.co.uk.
This information is for pupils joining the Senior School. For information about joining the Sixth Form click here.
Information for pupils currently at RGS Prep.

Visit Us
We hold small group tours in the Trinity term and our Open Day takes place in October every year.
Our Senior Admissions Process
1. Registration
All students must be registered to sit our entrance examination. Please complete the form here along with payment of the non-refundable registration fee.
Registration deadlines apply for each academic year.
If your child is currently in Year 7 or 8 please contact the Head of Admissions, Mrs Kathryn Sweet, on 01483 880 600 or by email at RGS-admissions@rgsg.co.uk before registering them.
2. Assessment
Our main entry points are:
11+ (Year 7)
The assessments for 11+ include:
A confidential reference from their current headteacher.
A short composition/English creative writing task.
3. Offers
Parents are notified of the outcome towards the middle of February, on a date agreed by all schools which are a member of the Trinity Group. Acceptances are required by early March.
4. What happens next?
If your child is offered a place, you will be invited to our Offer Holders’ Event in February. This allows parents and children to meet more of the staff body and current students and ask any outstanding questions. For those who accept their places, they are invited to our New Students’ Reception Afternoon.

Special Educational Needs
The RGS adopts an inclusive policy and students with Special Educational Needs are offered the opportunity to join the School if they satisfy the School’s selection procedures. Parents may be asked to contribute to any special resources. Students with Special Educational Needs will have access to the whole school curriculum and be fully integrated into the School. Exceptional circumstances, which may affect such access, will be dealt with on an individual basis in consultation with the Head of Learning Support, Head of Year, Deputy Heads, parents and the student themselves.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery in Guildford, Surrey | RGS Prep (ages 3 to 4)
pageCache.text:
RGS Nursery is a warm, welcoming nursery school in Guildford for children from the age of three, and the very first step of a Royal Grammar School education. As a private nursery in Guildford, part of RGS Prep, in the heart of the town we combine the care and encouragement young children need with all the reassurance of belonging to a much larger school. Here, every child feels happy, secure and known. Time in our Nursery sees children flourish and thrive, growing in confidence, making their first friendships and building the learning habits that will guide them throughout their education.
From September 2027, RGS becomes fully co-educational, and our Nursery and Reception (Shell) will welcome girls and boys together from the very start.
For families joining us in the early years, it means your child will grow up as part of an inclusive, forward-looking school community from their very first day, with the same warm welcome, high expectations and sense of belonging that have defined RGS for more than 500 years.
We welcome families from across Guildford and the surrounding Surrey towns and villages, including Godalming, Cranleigh, Woking, Cobham, Farnham and Shalford.
Our curriculum
From the moment a pupil joins RGS Prep, they embark on a journey towards becoming tenacious, imaginative, and self-aware individuals. Our curriculum is designed to instil positive habits and attitudes, and to develop our pupils as eager and resilient learners with a love of learning that will last a lifetime.
Nursery
In our Nursery school in Guildford, the timetable is predominantly driven by the children’s interests, featuring child-led learning and outdoor activities in our dedicated outdoor classroom.
Pupils enjoy a diverse range of activities which promote development across many important areas:
Our classrooms are stocked with open-ended resources, stimulating creativity and imaginative play. With a focus on nurturing each child’s individuality, we create an environment where the possibilities are endless, limited only by their imagination.
Communication and language
Physical development
Personal, social, and emotional development
Literacy
Mathematics
Understanding the world
Expressive arts and design
Reception (Shell)
Reception, known at RGS Prep as Shell, builds naturally on the Nursery year and marks the start of a child’s more structured learning journey. As one of the leading independent primary schools in Surrey, we blend plenty of play-based discovery with the first, gentle steps into formal learning.
Children continue to enjoy a huge variety of learning through fun-based resources, alongside more structured elements including phonics, handwriting, an introduction to numbers, mathematical language and early problem-solving.
Every child in Shell also enjoys a weekly Spanish lesson; dedicated music, art and drama taught by our subject specialists; PE on the extensive Prep School grounds; and a weekly swimming lesson.
Building friendships and collaboration
Our buddy system ensures that our youngest pupils form friendships with those in Years 1 and 2 and encourages independence and peer learning, enhancing language development and interpersonal skills.
A pupils join one of four Houses when they join RGS Prep, and many activities are organised throughout the year to ensure pupils form friendships and collaborate throughout the year groups.
Throughout our community, a strong emphasis is placed on our School Values of inclusivity, scholarship, integrity, respect, courage and collaboration.
Our Nursery offers a nurturing, well-resourced environment with dedicated Nursery teachers and teaching assistants . Our Nursery day begins at 9.00am (with drop off from 8.00am) and runs on a school day, although early pick up is possible from 2.00pm.
We accept the Surrey Early Years funding entitlement for eligible families, click here for more details, and wraparound care is available before and after the school day.
A typical day balances child-led discovery in our dedicated outdoor classroom with focused activities across the seven areas of learning, plus specialist input in music, PE and Spanish. The best way to see it for yourself is to come along to one of our Toddler Time sessions — an informal chance for you and your child to explore the Nursery together.
Visiting our Nursery in Guildford
Our Pre-Prep and Prep Schools in Guildford
Our younger children are based at our dedicated Pre-Prep department on Aldersey Road from Nursery to Year 2. This is a small and nurturing setting. When they reach Year 3 children move across the road into the larger and well-equipped RGS Prep site on Maori Road, Guildford, GU1 2EL. Both RGS Pre-Prep and Prep schools are within easy reach of central Guildford and the A3.
Children join our Nursery in the September after they turn three, and Reception (Shell) in the September after they turn four. The Nursery day runs from 8.25am to 3.10pm, with wraparound care available from 7.30am through to 6.30pm. See our School Day for a full timetable.

Nursery FAQs
What ages does the RGS Nursery take?
Children can join our Nursery in the September after their third birthday, and Reception (Shell) in the September after their fourth birthday.
Where is the Nursery based?
Our Nursery is part of RGS Prep in Guildford, Surrey, welcoming families from across Guildford and the surrounding area.
What are the Nursery hours?
The Nursery day runs from 8.25am to 3.10pm, with wraparound care available from 7.30am through to 6.30pm.
Do you offer funded or free childcare hours?
Yes. All 3 and 4 year olds are eligible for 15 hours a week of free childcare (Universal Funding) which is credited to your school bill. Some parents may also be eligible for Working Parent Entitlement. This is an extra 15 hours a week on top of your 15 hours a week Universal Funding. Please enquire with our Admissions team to find out about eligibility.
How much are Nursery fees?
The registration fee is £120 for UK families. Current termly fees are shown on our Fees page.
How do I register my child?
Simply complete the online registration form on our Register Now page and pay the registration fee.
Do you offer wraparound care?
Yes. We run a Breakfast Club from 7.30am and After School Care until 6.30pm, Monday to Friday.
When are your open days?
We hold Open Mornings in March, June and September, plus Toddler Time sessions in the Spring. For more information and to book go to our Visit Us page.
